# Job Card

The canonical open-role block: a category badge, the role title, a one-line summary and a meta tier of location, employment type and salary band. Renders as a chrome-less row or a bordered card.

```tsx
<JobCard variant="card">
  <JobCardContent>
    <Badge variant="success">Marketing</Badge>
    <JobCardTitle>Senior Graphic Designer</JobCardTitle>
    <JobCardDescription>
      Lead creative projects to elevate brand identity and visual storytelling.
    </JobCardDescription>
    <JobCardMeta>
      <JobCardMetaItem icon={<JobCardFlag country="US" />}>San Francisco, CA</JobCardMetaItem>
      <JobCardMetaItem icon={<CalendarBlank />}>Full-time</JobCardMetaItem>
      <JobCardMetaItem icon={<Money />}>
        <span className="tabular-nums">$80,000 – $120,000</span>
      </JobCardMetaItem>
    </JobCardMeta>
  </JobCardContent>
  <JobCardAction>
    <Button variant="outline">Apply</Button>
  </JobCardAction>
</JobCard>
```

## Installation

```bash
# One-time setup (tokens + lib helpers)
npx koalaui-cli init

# Add this component (its dependencies come along)
npx koalaui-cli add job-card
```

Manual: run `npm install radix-ui tailwind-variants tailwind-merge`, then copy the source into `components/ui/job-card/` and adjust the import paths to your project. Components pull `cn` from `lib/utils`, the `tv` wrapper from `lib/tv`, and (for multi-part components) `createContext` from `lib/create-context`.

## Usage

Compose the parts you need and omit the rest: there is no `showX` prop anywhere on this component. A role with no summary simply leaves out `JobCardDescription`; a board that links whole rows instead of showing a button leaves out `JobCardAction`. The eyebrow is an ordinary `Badge` dropped as the first child of `JobCardContent`, so it takes any tone in the Badge scale.

## Variants

`plain` (the default) is chrome-less: the row sits flush on whatever holds it, and the list that owns it paints the hairline between rows. `card` gives the role a box of its own: the boundary and nothing else, drawn straight on the page ground with no fill behind it, and with an inset ring rather than a border so the corner stays concentric with the radius inside it.

```tsx
<JobCard variant="plain">…</JobCard>
<JobCard variant="card">…</JobCard>
```

## Layouts

`split` (the default) rides the action against the right edge, vertically centred. `stacked` drops it below the content, which is what a card in a narrow column wants. `inline` is the table shape: title and meta share one line, and the meta becomes equal-width auto columns so the same template repeats on every row and the columns line up down the whole board. Both row layouts start as a stacked column and only become a row at their breakpoint (`sm`for split, `md` for inline), so an action never strands itself in the corner of a narrow frame.

```tsx
<JobCard layout="split">…</JobCard>
<JobCard layout="stacked" variant="card">…</JobCard>
<JobCard layout="inline">…</JobCard>
```

## Divided rows

`divided` turns a stack of plain rows into a board: a hairline under each one and the vertical band that gives the row its height. It is a rule of its own rather than a `border-b`, so it stays straight even under a rounded interactive row. Compose it as a real list, one `<li>` per role and no gap between them: the hairline is the separation, and the trailing rule is dropped from the last list item so the board does not close with a line under nothing.

```tsx
<ul className="flex flex-col">
  {roles.map((role) => (
    <li key={role.title}>
      <JobCard divided>…</JobCard>
    </li>
  ))}
</ul>
```

## Interactive rows

Pass `interactive` (with `asChild` and an `<a>` child) when the whole row opens the role. A plain interactive row pulls its hover fill back into a detached rounded panel so the wash does not bleed to the container edge, while the text stays flush-aligned, and the hairline pulls in by the same amount so it never overhangs the text. There is no press scale: a row that shrinks pulls its fill off the edges it sits against and starts reading as a floating tile, so the press is a deepening fill instead.

```tsx
<li>
  <JobCard divided interactive asChild>
    <a href="#senior-graphic-designer">…</a>
  </JobCard>
</li>
```

## Any action, not just a button

`JobCardAction` is a plain slot, so a board that wants to show who is hiring drops an `AvatarGroup` into it instead of a button. Nothing about the recipe changes.

```tsx
{/* Pass the same size to the group AND to every child: the group picks its overlap
    from its own size, so unsized 40px avatars under a 32px overlap stack wrong. */}
<JobCardAction>
  <AvatarGroup size="sm">
    {team.map((p) => (
      <AvatarRoot key={p.name} size="sm">
        <AvatarImage src={p.src} alt={p.name} />
        <AvatarFallback>{p.name[0]}</AvatarFallback>
      </AvatarRoot>
    ))}
  </AvatarGroup>
</JobCardAction>
```

## API reference

### JobCard

The root `<div>`. Forwards all native `<div>` props.

- `variant`: `"plain"` (default) | `"card"`.
- `layout`: `"split"` (default) | `"stacked"` | `"inline"`.
- `divided`: `boolean`; the hairline rule under the row, plus the vertical band that gives the row its height. A divided list has no gap between rows by definition, so the row supplies its own. Expects a list-item wrapper: the trailing rule is dropped from the last `<li>`, not from the card itself.
- `interactive`: `boolean`; hover/press/focus affordance for a row that is itself a link.
- `asChild`: `boolean`; render via Radix Slot, e.g. as an `<li>` or `<a>`.

### JobCardMetaItem

One meta fact. Forwards native `<span>` props.

- `icon`: `ReactNode`; the leading 20px glyph. A node rather than a component type so one item can pass a Phosphor icon and the next a `JobCardFlag`.

### JobCardFlag

A country flag cropped into a ringed circle, sized to the meta glyph and marked decorative (the country is already spelled out beside it).

- `country`: `string`; an ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code, matching the `iso2` field of the shared countries dataset.

### JobCardContent, JobCardTitle, JobCardDescription, JobCardMeta, JobCardAction

The block parts: the text column, the role title (a `<div>` by default, with `asChild` for a real heading), the muted summary, the meta tier, and the trailing action slot. Each forwards its native element props, and each is optional.

## FAQ

### When should I use JobCard instead of List or Card?

Reach for JobCard when the row is an open role. List is the compact settings or member row: text-sm, a truncating title, and meta pinned right on the same line. JobCard is a marketing-scale block whose meta is a third tier under the summary and is allowed to wrap. Card is the generic surface with no opinion about its contents.

### How do I hide the summary or the apply button?

Omit the part. Every piece of the anatomy is a separate component you compose, so a role with no summary simply leaves out JobCardDescription and a board with no button leaves out JobCardAction. There is no showX prop.

### Why does the card variant use a ring instead of a border, and no fill?

A 1px border sits outside the padding box, so it enlarges the element and breaks the concentric relationship between the outer corner and the radius of anything nested inside it. An inset ring paints in the same place without changing the box. It carries no background either: a grid of filled panels reads as chrome competing with the roles, and on the dark themes the card token is light enough to turn every row into a grey slab. Because it introduces no new ground, it deliberately does not redeclare --surface, so a nested Badge or Button keeps resolving the page's.

### How do the inline layout columns line up across rows?

The inline layout pins the title to a fixed first column and turns the meta tier into equal-width auto columns from md up. Every row uses the identical template inside the same container width, so the columns align down the whole board without needing a grid on the list itself, and each card stays a self-contained unit. The title has to be fixed rather than flexible: two flexible siblings split the row in half whatever is in them, which hands half the width to a two-word role and squeezes the meta until it truncates.

### Why does a divided row need an <li> around it?

Because the trailing rule keys off the list item. List and Activity Feed render their own <li> and hang the divider on it, so they can simply hide the rule on the last child. Job Card does not render the <li> — it also goes into card grids, scroll rails and standalone previews — so the list that owns it supplies one, and inside that wrapper the card is always its own parent's last child. Hiding on the card's own :last-child would therefore blank the hairline on every row of the board rather than only the final one. Compose a divided board as a real list: <ul className="flex flex-col"> with one <li> per role and no gap, since the hairline is the separation.

### Why does a divided row carry padding?

Because nothing else can. A list of divided rows stacks them with no gap — the hairline is the separation — so the row's own vertical padding is the only thing giving it height. Without it a 40px Apply button fills the row edge to edge and lands flush on the hairline above and below. An interactive row restates a slightly tighter band, so its hover panel sits closer to the text.

### Why is there no press scale on an interactive row?

A row sits flush to the edges of the surface holding it. Shrinking it on press pulls the fill away from those edges and the row starts reading as a floating tile. The press is a deepening fill instead: hover lands on a half-strength wash, active on the full one.

### Where do the flags come from?

JobCardFlag indexes country-flag-icons by ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code, the same way CountrySelect and PhoneInput do, so the codes match the iso2 field of the shared countries dataset. It renders nothing for an unknown code rather than throwing.
